# `enum-value-added`

Enum value added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `enum-value-added` (both directions), `enum-value-added-in-request`, `enum-value-added-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A value was added to an enum.

## Why this default

In requests: old clients never send it. In responses: clients with exhaustive switches or strict enum types fail on the new value. A warning, because tolerant clients are fine.

## Example

From test case [`enum-value-added`](../../test/cases/enum-value-added/): A value added to a response enum: exhaustive clients may break.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
            - a
            - b
+           - c
```

Findings:

- `enum-value-added-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `honour-open-hint` | `true` | Treat enums marked `x-api-diff: { enum: open }` as `info`. |
| `open-extensions` | `[]` | Other extensions that mean "open enum", e.g. `[x-extensible-enum]`. |

```yaml
rules:
  enum-value-added: warn
```

## How to fix

Mark enums that clients must treat as open with `x-api-diff: { enum: open }`, or only send the new value to clients that support it.
